source: Sheet1 formulas O3 (Multiplier) and Q3 (Tonnage); material list from data validation on L3

materials.name: Steel
materials.note: Default/else branch in Q3 and O3 (any material that is not Stainless Steel or Aluminum)

clearance.description: Total die clearance as a fraction of material thickness. Die = MROUND(thickness*multiplier + punch, 1/32). Use the first row where thickness >= minThk. 'sheet' holds Nick's original O3 values.

changes.why: Nick confirmed the 12% at 0.25-0.499" was a typo. All aluminum steps now use Mate's aluminum piercing chart mapped onto Nick's thickness steps: 15% under 0.098", 20% for 0.098-0.197", 25% over 0.197" (Mate's top tier, so it also covers 0.5"+).

sources.label: Mate Precision Technologies, Technical Solutions Guide, Die Clearance Chart (total clearance, % of thickness)
Cleveland Steel Tool Catalog 103, Clearance Guide (ironworker tooling)
sources.summary: Soft aluminum 10%; stainless 18%; mild steel fixed steps: 1/32" for 3/16-15/32", 1/16" for 1/2-23/32", 3/32" for 3/4"+, 1/8" for 1"+ (about 12.5% at most common thicknesses).

sources.label: Cleveland Steel Tool, Die Clearance & Tonnage Chart (mild steel)

review: Steel (12/16/20/24/26%): runs about 4-6 points below Mate's mild-steel chart (20/25/30%) and about 1.5-2x CST's ironworker chart (about 12.5%). It falls between the two. Not changed.
Stainless (20/25/30/35/35%): matches Mate's stainless tiers closely (20-35%). It is well above CST's flat 18%. Not changed.
Aluminum at 0.5"+ was 35% in the sheet, more than steel. Both sources put aluminum below steel, so it is now 25%. That still sits 1 point above steel's 24% at 0.5-0.749".

tonnageSources.label: Nick's sheet Q3 (round): shear psi x thk x pi x D / 2000
Cleveland Steel Tool Catalog 103, Punching Tonnage Guide (shaped holes use the perimeter)
Mate Technical Solutions Guide (tonnage = perimeter x thickness x shear strength)
